full_judgment:
Mohammad Fazlul Karim J:- Delay is condoned. This application under Article 103 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh is directed against the judgment and order dated the 18th day of May, 2009 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Misc. Case No. 1576 of 2008 discharging the Rule. 

 2. The facts involved in the case, in short, are that the accused, Jamal Uddin for his business purpose on 14.08.2002 took TK. 5,00,000.00(five lacs) from the complainant, Dr. A. B. M. Morshed Alam Chowdhury as loan at his house but the accused did not repay the said money to him in time; as a result, he requested the: accused to pay the same and at one stage of request the accused gave a current cheque amount of TK. 5,00,000.00(five lacs) and after receiving the said cheque the complainant on the same day deposited the same to his account in National Bank Ltd. Choumuhani Branch, Noakhali but the cheque was dishonored with a noting that the fund is insufficient and thereafter, the complainant informed the same to the accused petitioner and the accused petitioner replied that required money was deposited and after that he deposited the cheque but the cheque was dishonored noting that the fund is insufficient on 18.02.2004. On request of the accused, complainant further deposited the cheque but the cheque was dishonored noting that the fund is insufficient on 24.02.2004. Having no other alternative on 04.03.2004 the complainant sent a legal notice through his Advocate stating all the facts to the accused petitioner with a request to pay the loan money to him within 7 days. After receiving the legal notice, the accused petitioner requested the complainant to deposit the cheque and the complainant again deposited the cheque but the cheque was dishonored noting that the fifth is insufficient on 04.04.2004. Thereafter, the complainant sent a legal notice through his Advocate on 04.04.2004 stating all the facts to the accused petitioner with a request to pay the .loan money to him but he refused to receive the notice. At last on 21.04.2004 the complainant further sent a legal notice through his Advocate stating all the facts to the accused with a request to pay the loan money to him within 7 days but the accused petitioner refused to receive the legal notice; as a result on 29.04.2004 the cause of action of the aforesaid case was arisen under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instrument Act, 1881. 

 3. Mr. A. Y. Moshiuzzaman learned Advocate, appearing for the Stationer submitted that the impugned proceedings against the accused petiole is barred by limitation, inasmuch kas, the first legal notice was is on 04.03.2004 but the case under action 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 was filed on 11.05.2004 and as such, the impugned proceeding hopelessly barred by limitation.
